stories.title: North American indices slip into correction as tech sell‑off erases Nasdaq’s 2026 gains
stories.summary: A sharp tech‑driven sell‑off hit North American markets on Friday, sending the Nasdaq Composite down 5.28% to 22,654.15 and wiping out its 2026 gains. The S&P 500 fell 3.59% to 6,918.45 and the Dow Jones Industrial Average dropped 1.85% to 48,188.18, moving all three indices into correction territory. AI‑related stocks such as Nvidia led the declines, while defensive names like UnitedHealth, Walmart and Johnson & Johnson posted gains.
stories.why: The drop highlights heightened volatility in the AI‑driven rally and may trigger portfolio re‑balancing.

stories.title: Russian cruise missile breaches Polish airspace, hits rural area
stories.summary: Poland said a Russian Kh‑101 cruise missile was one of three objects that entered its airspace early on Friday and struck a rural area near the village of Nowy Lipowiec, about 50 km from the Ukrainian border. No injuries or damage were reported. The incident occurred while Western military exercises were taking place in the region, and Russia has not commented.
stories.why: It underscores the risk of the Ukraine conflict spilling over into NATO territory.

stories.previousSummary: Poland says a Russian cruise missile was among three objects that violated its airspace early on Friday, with Prime Minister Donald Tusk saying it did not appear to be an accident when Western military exercises were taking place in the region. Defence Minister Wladyslaw Kosiniak-Kamysz said the Kh-101 missile hit a rural area at Nowy Lipowiec in southeastern Poland about 50km (31 miles) from the Ukrainian border.

stories.summary: Even older chips retain value — according to Compute Credit Index Research , some H100s are selling for about half of their original cost basis from 2023, while some H200 configurations are selling for the same price they did when introduced in 2024. stories.title: RBI expected to raise repo rate to 5.75% in Dec, 6% in Feb, poll shows
stories.summary: A Reuters poll cited by the Economic Times indicates the Reserve Bank of India will increase its policy repo rate by 25 basis points to 5.75% in December and again by 25 basis points to 6% in February. The hikes are prompted by inflation moving above the RBI’s 6% tolerance band, driven by higher energy costs and uneven monsoon rainfall.
stories.why: RBI action or currency-market developments can affect rupee volatility, hedging costs and foreign-exchange conditions for businesses and investors.
